title: Disk Steward macOS evidence monitor
reason: Backfilled from an existing completed lifecycle.

intent.statement: A macOS user can leave Disk Steward running as a lightweight menu-bar app, understand material disk growth, export trustworthy evidence for Codex or Claude, and query the same evidence through a read-only local MCP integration.

success_evidence.description: A signed-development build launches as a menu-bar utility; left-click opens a compact status board and right-click exposes Export, Settings, About, and Quit.
The app measures whole-volume capacity while collecting bounded detailed evidence for configured roots and registered agent process trees.
Evidence identifies path, time, size delta, actor and agent session when observable, and labels exact, tool-linked, inferred, or unknown attribution without guessing.
A user can export a portable, integrity-manifested evidence bundle containing a concise Codex brief and machine-readable detailed records.
Codex and Claude can query sanitized evidence through the same read-only local MCP executable without rescanning the disk.
Monitoring remains useful without restricted privileges and enables exact Endpoint Security provenance only when entitlement and user authorization are available.
The app records no file contents, provides explicit privacy exclusions and retention limits, and performs no deletion or cleanup mutation in this intent.
Automated and reproducible checks demonstrate buildability, evidence correctness, regression safety, bounded idle resource use, and recovery from unavailable monitoring components.

constraints: Use a native Swift-first macOS architecture and keep the continuously running footprint bounded.
Prefer macOS 13 or newer, Swift 6, AppKit for status-item mouse behavior, SwiftUI for presented UI, SQLite for local evidence, and the official Swift MCP SDK.
Treat Endpoint Security entitlement approval as an external dependency and preserve a functional FSEvents/snapshot fallback.
Keep MCP read-only and avoid an externally reachable HTTP listener.
Do not persist file contents, secrets, or unbounded raw write-event streams.
Every attribution statement must carry method and confidence.
Generated evidence and databases must have deterministic retention and size controls.
non_goals: Automatic deletion, cache purging, process termination, or destructive MCP tools.
Cloud synchronization, accounts, telemetry, or a hosted backend.
Detailed monitoring of external, network, Time Machine, or cloud-placeholder volumes by default.
Guaranteeing Apple Endpoint Security entitlement approval.

assumptions.statement: The development machine has a compatible Xcode and Swift toolchain for a macOS 13+ Swift 6 application.
A native project layout can package the menu app, a local MCP executable, and later a system extension without introducing a second application language.
Endpoint Security entitlement may be unavailable or delayed, so exact system-wide attribution cannot be a prerequisite for the standard product path.
A stdio MCP executable can serve both Codex and Claude while delegating sanitized queries to the local app-owned evidence service.

decisions.question: What is the smallest honest delivery ladder from an empty repository?
decisions.choice: Deliver four cumulative runnable increments: snapshot/export menu app; persistent evidence recorder; agent-queryable MCP integration; advanced exact provenance with fallback.
alternatives: Treat project scaffolding as an increment
decisions.rationale: Each selected rung gives the user a launchable, meaningful scenario and isolates storage, integration, and restricted-entitlement risks behind independent gates.

decisions.question: Which application stack should be primary?
decisions.choice: Swift 6 with a small AppKit NSStatusItem shell, SwiftUI presentation, a shared Swift core, and SQLite persistence.
alternatives: Tauri with a Rust core and web UI
Pure MenuBarExtra without AppKit status-item event handling
decisions.rationale: The selected stack directly accesses macOS monitoring, service-management, signing, and menu APIs while minimizing continuous runtime and cross-language boundaries.

decisions.question: How broadly should monitoring persist detailed evidence?
decisions.choice: Track whole-volume capacity everywhere accessible, but persist detailed evidence only for configured roots, registered agent process trees, and bounded investigation windows.
alternatives: Scan the whole disk only when asked
decisions.rationale: The hybrid model preserves unexplained-growth detection and agent attribution without creating an unbounded privacy and resource burden.

decisions.question: How should Codex and Claude access evidence?
decisions.choice: Bundle one read-only Swift MCP stdio executable that delegates to the app-owned evidence service over a protected local IPC boundary.
alternatives: Expose a persistent localhost HTTP server
Give each agent direct SQLite access
Maintain separate Codex and Claude implementations
decisions.rationale: One connector minimizes duplication and attack surface while keeping database ownership, sanitization, and retention inside the application.

decisions.question: How should exact system-wide attribution depend on Endpoint Security?
decisions.choice: Implement it as an advanced capability with explicit confidence semantics and retain a useful FSEvents/snapshot fallback.
alternatives: Block the whole product on entitlement approval
decisions.rationale: Entitlement approval is external and cannot be guaranteed; the product must remain honest and useful in its absence.

decisions.question: Should the first product intent perform cleanup?
decisions.choice: No; it will explain, export, and recommend while all MCP tools remain read-only.
decisions.rationale: Evidence trust and attribution accuracy must be established before introducing destructive operations.

demonstrable_outcomes.title: Launchable disk snapshot and export utility
demonstrable_outcomes.summary: A user can launch a native menu-bar utility, inspect current capacity, use the required click behaviors, and export a truthful current snapshot.

evidence: All six primary children—RESEARCH-101, CONTRACT-101, TASK-110, TASK-111, TASK-112, and GATE-190—have verification=passed and health=clear.

GATE-190 retained a legible native status-board render, a live accessory-app launch report with distinct click routes and required menu, a deterministic parseable export fixture, matching integrity hashes, and privacy checks forbidding file contents.

demonstrable_outcomes.title: Persistent bounded evidence recorder
demonstrable_outcomes.summary: The menu-bar app records and explains material growth using whole-volume metrics and targeted detailed monitoring with bounded retention.

evidence: GATE-290 independently passed with complete coverage of CONTRACT-101, both prior increment foundations, TASK-210 through TASK-213, and inherited OUTCOME-010 proof.

A user-facing settings model and view control watched/excluded roots, bounded retention, thresholds, sample interval, pause/resume, investigation window, and launch at login; the existing menu-bar popover presents live state and export.

The integrated fixture establishes a baseline, writes watched and outside-root allocations, records only the watched path as inferred detail, preserves outside growth as unknown, and emits one threshold-crossing signal.
SQLite WAL recovery, hard size ceilings, raw-to-hourly-to-daily retention, anomaly preservation, consistent backup, and export of retained rollups all pass focused and integrated tests.
The complete time-bounded bundle is deterministic for fixtures, schema-valid, hash-verifiable, concurrency-consistent, redacted, explicit about missing attribution, and human-readable.

The current 54-test suite and executable smoke re-establish the original live snapshot, compact status board, click routing/menu actions, and deterministic snapshot export against the current candidate.
No cleanup/deletion tool was added; no file contents or environment are captured; unavailable FSEvents degrades to scheduled sampling; unknown attribution is never guessed.

demonstrable_outcomes.title: Agent-queryable storage evidence
demonstrable_outcomes.summary: Codex and Claude can query the same sanitized local evidence and exported records without independently digging through the disk.

evidence: OUTCOME-020, CONTRACT-301, TASK-310, TASK-311, TASK-312, and GATE-390 are all verified passed with clear health.

The shared connector completes MCP initialization and discovery, advertises seven closed read-only tools plus two resources, separates protocol/execution errors, sanitizes results, and enforces response bounds.
Authenticated private-socket registration links one active session and workspace; the end-to-end gate attributes its retained artifact only as inferred and preserves the no-proof limitation.
Validated Codex plugin/TOML and Claude JSON paths install, upgrade, diagnose, and uninstall in isolated roots while retaining unrelated configuration and evidence.
MCP and app-service exports have equal bounded summary and event detail for the same request, preserving the existing integrity-manifested export semantics.

No destructive MCP tool exists, delete_file is rejected, cleanup candidates require review, forbidden exact keys are absent, credentials are not bundled, and unavailable app state fails with recovery guidance rather than invented evidence.

The current 83-test suite repeats volume snapshot, menu-bar routes/status/export, persistent monitoring, notification, retention, recovery, redaction, and evidence-bundle scenarios in the same candidate.

demonstrable_outcomes.title: Advanced trustworthy provenance
demonstrable_outcomes.summary: The running product distinguishes exact and inferred process-to-file attribution, remains useful without privileged monitoring, and satisfies privacy and resource controls.

evidence: OUTCOME-030, RESEARCH-401, CONTRACT-401, TASK-410, TASK-411, RISK-420, and GATE-490 are all verified with passing audits.

Normalized privileged fixture events establish exact create, grow, and rename only with complete process/file identity, size measurement, timing, operation, path, and gap-free linkage; PID/start ancestry can link one authenticated task.
Denied, pending, unavailable, not-entitled, crashed, overloaded, dropped, and gapped privileged states retain the standard snapshot/FSEvents path and never claim exact attribution.

The final gate relaunches the actual menu-bar executable and MCP connector, repeats live snapshot, status board, settings, watched/excluded monitoring, integrity-manifested export, provenance query, and stopped-service recovery journeys.

Privacy property tests, exclusion controls, bounded retention/history/queues, 100,000-event overload accounting, safe uninstall recovery, and fail-closed release preflight pass without adding deletion or telemetry.

Fixture exactness is explicitly separated from unavailable Apple entitlement and signed-host evidence. Signing, notarization, live activation lifecycle, and signed-artifact resource measurements remain visible release gates.

turning_points: Decision: Deliver four cumulative runnable increments: snapshot/export menu app; persistent evidence recorder; agent-queryable MCP integration; advanced exact provenance with fallback — Each selected rung gives the user a launchable, meaningful scenario and isolates storage, integration, and restricted-entitlement risks behind independent gates

Decision: Swift 6 with a small AppKit NSStatusItem shell, SwiftUI presentation, a shared Swift core, and SQLite persistence — The selected stack directly accesses macOS monitoring, service-management, signing, and menu APIs while minimizing continuous runtime and cross-language boundaries

Decision: Track whole-volume capacity everywhere accessible, but persist detailed evidence only for configured roots, registered agent process trees, and bounded investigation windows — The hybrid model preserves unexplained-growth detection and agent attribution without creating an unbounded privacy and resource burden

Decision: Bundle one read-only Swift MCP stdio executable that delegates to the app-owned evidence service over a protected local IPC boundary — One connector minimizes duplication and attack surface while keeping database ownership, sanitization, and retention inside the application

Decision: Implement it as an advanced capability with explicit confidence semantics and retain a useful FSEvents/snapshot fallback — Entitlement approval is external and cannot be guaranteed; the product must remain honest and useful in its absence
Decision: No; it will explain, export, and recommend while all MCP tools remain read-only — Evidence trust and attribution accuracy must be established before introducing destructive operations
human_story.ending: The intent ended with all required primary evidence verified.
